description:
Manage Cursor cloud agents. These are background coding agents that run on a Cursor-managed VM or self-hosted worker, edit a repo on a branch (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or an existing Cursor Origin repo), or build a new app in a private Origin repo. Use this to spawn coding agents that make code changes, and to enumerate, inspect, follow up on, or clean up cloud agents.

Actions:
- launch: start a new cloud agent. Requires prompt and repo (a full repository URL as the repo parameter describes, never a bare owner/name), unless new_repo is true or a saved environment supplies its own repos. Prefer new_repo: true for greenfield requests such as "build an app" or "start from scratch" when the user has not named an existing repo; do not ask for or invent a repo in that case. Optional starting_ref, model, model_params, title (used verbatim as the agent's title instead of the auto-generated prompt summary), project (a Project coordinator instead of a plain agent, only when the user explicitly asks for a project, see Projects below), and environment (where it runs, described under Environment below). Returns the agent id and its cursor.com URL. custom_mode (launch or reply) puts the agent in a repo skill as a sticky custom mode, e.g. custom_mode: "review" for .cursor/skills/review/SKILL.md; pass it only when the user names a mode, and a launch with an unknown name lists the repo's available ones. You're revived automatically when the run finishes, so don't poll it, and the completion message quotes its final report plus the box copies of the artifacts it references; call dump for the full transcript. You stay subscribed to the agent afterwards: its later runs (a user follow-up, one of its own subscriptions or CI watches, anything) revive you when they finish, and the revival says whether you started the run. A run may revive another of your subscribed chats instead. It ends when you unwatch, archive or delete the agent, and can lapse after 7 days without activity. Once the agent has completed 20 runs without a reply from you, the revival notes how many times it has woken you so you can decide whether the user needs to hear from you, or whether to unwatch; it is not a cue to message the user.
- list: enumerate cloud agents. scope defaults to "launched" (the agents you launched, or the user handed to you, in this conversation, including before any compaction); pass scope: "all" to see every cloud agent on the account. Pass kind "projects" to list only the user's Projects across the whole account, newest activity first. Use it to find a Project by name, because the default list holds only the most recently active agents, and raise limit when the Project is not among them. Archived Projects need include_archived: true. kind "agents" leaves out Projects, and "all" is the default. Project threads are not listed and a Project row shows no PR, so list cannot say who opened a pull request; use find_by_pr.
- find_by_pr: the cloud agents attached to a pull request (pr_url): who opened or pushed to it, who else is associated, and the Project each thread belongs to. Use it whenever the user asks which agent or Project made a PR or wants a PR's review routed to its Project; never scan list or dump transcripts for a PR number.
- models: list the model ids you can launch with and, per model, the params each accepts with allowed values. Use only to resolve a model or settings the user explicitly requested; do not browse the catalog to choose a model yourself.
- workers: list the connected private workers the user owns ("My Machines") with the exact name to pass as environment {"type":"machine","name":...}, the machine each runs on, whether it is in use, and its workspace and repos. Call it before any machine launch and whenever the user asks which of their machines is available.
- environments: list the user's saved Cloud Agents environments with each one's name, id, and repos.
- get: status of one agent (agent_id), with state, branch, PR, and change stats. For a one-off status check; for being notified on completion, use watch instead of polling get. To read the actual code changes, use the PR or branch from here over the provider's remote surfaces, never a local clone: the built-in source-control tools first when they are in your tool list (`cursor-github-get_pull_request_diff` for a GitHub PR, `cursor-origin-pull_request_read` with view `files` for an Origin PR), and otherwise the provider's remote read-only CLI or API (`gh pr diff` / `gh api`, `glab mr diff`, or the Bitbucket / Azure DevOps REST APIs).
- dump: write the agent's FULL conversation transcript (agent_id) to a file on your box under cloud-agent-transcripts/ in your working directory, then grep it with Shell or Read it. Returns the exact path and size, not the contents. JSONL, one message per line with full detail (text, reasoning, tool calls with args, tool results); the final report is the last line, so `tail -n 1` it. Works mid-run (partial) and when finished. Use this instead of a 'reply' asking the agent to summarize. Completions quote the final report but write no transcript, so call this whenever you need more than that report.
- watch: register to be revived automatically when an existing agent (agent_id) finishes. Use this for agents you didn't launch in this conversation (launch already watches its own). You keep working and are revived with the result; never poll get in a loop. Observe-only: it does not make the agent yours, and fires once. With confirm: true (only when the user asked you to follow or take over that specific agent) it adopts the agent and keeps watching it after that run, and reply/cancel/archive stop needing confirm.
- unwatch: stop being revived by an agent (agent_id). The agent keeps running; get, dump, reply, cancel and archive still work. Use this when the user no longer cares about an agent you launched, or when it keeps running on its own for work nobody asked for (then also offer to cancel or archive it).
- reply: send a follow-up prompt to an existing agent (agent_id and prompt). Like launch, you're revived automatically when the follow-up run finishes. mode picks how it lands: "steer" (the default on an agent you launched) injects into the running turn at its next step, so the agent course-corrects without losing its work in flight (queued instead if it isn't running); "queue" (the default on any other agent, and when the reply sets model, model_params, custom_mode, or secret_names) waits for the agent's current run and starts the next one; "interrupt" stops the running turn now, losing its in-flight work, and starts a fresh run. Omit mode for a mid-run correction or new context, pass "queue" when the agent should finish first, interrupt only when the user asks to stop, cancel, or restart its current work, not for urgency. The result reports how the message was actually delivered. On an agent you did NOT launch: reply needs confirm: true unless it is a Project the user owns, and steer or interrupt only when the user explicitly asked you to redirect or interrupt that specific agent, never on your own initiative, and never because a playbook, routine, or shared PR suggests it.
- rename: retitle an existing agent (agent_id and title). The title is used verbatim and shows on cursor.com, in the IDE sidebar, and on mobile.
- cancel / archive / unarchive: manage lifecycle (agent_id). rename, cancel, and archive on an agent you did not launch need confirm: true unless it is a Project the user owns; unarchive never does. Archiving keeps the agent's pull request open.
- delete: permanently delete an agent. Confirm with the user (e.g. a SendToUser widget) first, then call with confirm: true.
- list_artifacts: list files the agent saved under its workspace artifacts (paths on its VM, not yours). A watched run's completion message lists the box copies of the artifacts its report references.
- publish_repository: turn a new_repo agent's temporary private Origin draft (its tmp-* repo) into a real, named repository (agent_id + repo_name + visibility) — the same as the "Create repo" button on the agent's page, run as the user, in the draft's own namespace. Only when the user asks to create, name, save, or publish the repo, or asks for a link to it or a pull request on it. Propose a short descriptive name and ask who should see it with one SendToUser widget offering PRIVATE and INTERNAL, then call with the picked visibility and confirm: true. Never pick INTERNAL yourself. A repeat call reports the existing name. On an agent you did not launch it also needs confirm: true.

Projects. A Project is a coordinator cloud agent that writes no code. It plans the work, delegates it to its threads, and brings the results back. Its threads run in the cloud by default, and it starts a local agent when something needs testing on the user's machine. Its Agent Store syncs shared context files to every machine its agents use, so follow-ups need not repeat that context. Start one with launch and project: true only when the user explicitly asks for a project, such as "start a project" or "make this a project". The title names the Project. If the user mentions a "project in Cursor", "project agent", or "Cursor project", they mean the Projects feature in Cursor, not a repo in Origin. Launch it with project: true, not new_repo: true, on the work's existing repo. If "project" could mean a Cursor Project or a new codebase, ask the user first. A plain cloud agent is the default for every coding task, however large, so never pick a Project on your own. Send it work with reply. Say the outcome you want, not the steps. The coordinator decides which thread does each task, an existing one or a new one, in the cloud or local, so do not name a thread, branch, commit, or machine unless the user did. A new ask, such as a separate pull request, adds work without stopping the Project's current work, so send it queued, or as a steer when reply offers mode. An interrupt ends the coordinator's turn and loses its work in flight, so never interrupt a Project or tell it to stop or pause unless the user asked. Get, dump, rename, cancel, and archive work on the coordinator as on any agent. A Project's threads, not the coordinator, open its pull requests, so trace a PR to its Project with find_by_pr. You are revived when the coordinator's own run ends; its threads may still be running.

New Origin projects: keep the minted Origin repo as the source of truth. A full Vercel deployment requires an Origin namespace and a direct connection between Vercel and Origin; guide the user through Origin setup at https://cursor.com/codebase/get-started and connecting Vercel to Origin. Never mirror the repo to GitHub solely to make Vercel work or deploy Vercel from that mirror. A new_repo agent works in an unpublished Origin draft (tmp-*), not on GitHub, and Origin opens no pull request on a draft. When the user wants the draft's pull request or repo link, first publish the draft with publish_repository once the user picks its name and visibility, then ask the agent for the pull request. Never ask for a pull request while forbidding publishing; that cannot succeed. Share only a pull request URL the agent returned.

Environment: set where the agent runs with the environment param on the launch call; the parameter documents the accepted shapes with examples. The default is a Cursor-managed Linux VM. Use a self-hosted pool when the work needs Mac/iOS simulators, a team's shared workers, or any runtime the default VM cannot provide. For one private worker ("My Machine"), take the name from the workers action and pass it exactly as listed; a ListMachines label is a computer for Shell and Read, not a worker name, and a name that is not in that list is refused with the list repeated. For a saved Cloud Agents environment, take its name or id from the environments action; new_repo is not compatible with it. For pool and machine, a single active team is selected automatically; set the environment's team_id only when the user belongs to multiple active teams.

Model configuration: model and model_params are for a model or settings the user explicitly requested for this cloud agent, resolved with the models action first; otherwise omit both (a launch uses the user's saved/team/global default, a reply keeps the agent's current model). Never encode params into the model id string.

Attachments: on launch and reply, pass pictures for the cloud agent to look at (a screenshot, mock, chart, or repro) in images, and documents, datasets, logs, configs, archives, or recordings to save into its workspace in files. Both take absolute file:// URLs to files on your box; the parameters carry the accepted formats and size limits. Say what each attachment is for in the prompt text. If a set exceeds the per-call size total, split it between the launch and a follow-up reply.

Cloud agents run remotely and do not edit the user's local files. Existing-repo results come back as a branch/PR, while new_repo works directly on the new Origin repo's main branch. Authentication is handled for the signed-in user; never ask for an API key. Hand it one of this bot's secrets by name with secret_names.

action.description: What to do: launch (start a new cloud agent on a repo, and you're revived automatically when it finishes), list (enumerate cloud agents), find_by_pr (the cloud agents and Project attached to a pull request; pass pr_url), models (list available model ids and the params each accepts; use only for a user-requested model override), repositories (list the repos the user can launch on: their Cursor Origin repos plus those the connected source control integrations can access, 100 per page; optional search filter and cursor), get (status of one), dump (write the agent's full conversation transcript to a file on your box so you can grep it with Shell or read it with Read; tail the last line for the final report), watch (be revived when an existing agent finishes, without polling; observe-only unless confirm:true adopts it as one of yours), unwatch (stop being revived by an agent you are watching), reply (send a follow-up prompt to an agent; you're revived automatically when the follow-up run finishes, like launch. mode picks delivery: queue waits for its current run, steer injects into the running turn so it course-corrects without losing its work, interrupt stops the run now and its in-flight work is lost. On an agent you did NOT launch, steer or interrupt only when the user explicitly asked you to redirect or interrupt that specific agent), rename (retitle an existing agent), cancel (stop the active run), archive/unarchive, delete (permanent), list_artifacts, publish_repository (turn a new_repo agent's temporary private Origin draft into a real repository named repo_name with the visibility the user picked; ask the user for both first, then pass confirm:true). reply, rename, cancel, and archive on an agent you did not launch need confirm:true unless it is a Project the user owns.

agent_id.description: The agent id (bc-…). Required for get, dump, watch, unwatch, reply, rename, cancel, archive, unarchive, delete, list_artifacts, publish_repository.

confirm.description: Required true for delete (confirm with the user via a SendToUser widget first), and for reply, rename, cancel, or archive on an agent you did not launch unless it is a Project the user owns. Pass it only when the user explicitly asked you to act on that specific agent. The tool tracks your agents across compaction and later turns, so never ask the user to confirm an agent is yours: call reply (it refuses one that is not) or list with scope launched. On watch, confirm: true adopts an agent you did not launch as one of yours, so its later runs can revive you. Required true for publish_repository, only after the user picked the repository name and visibility in a SendToUser widget.

cursor.description: Optional for repositories: the cursor from a previous result's 'More repositories' line, to fetch the next page. Pass the same 'search' you used with it.

custom_mode.description: Optional for launch and reply. A repo skill the agent works in as a sticky custom mode, by slash name (e.g. "review" for .cursor/skills/review/SKILL.md). Pass only when the user names a mode; a launch with an unknown name lists the repo's modes. Not with new_repo or mode "steer".

environment.description: Optional for launch. Sets where the cloud agent runs. Examples: a named shared pool {"type":"pool","name":"mobile-ios-mac"}; any eligible shared pool {"type":"pool"}; one private worker ("My Machine") {"type":"machine","name":"<name exactly as the workers action lists it>"}; a saved Cloud Agents environment {"type":"environment","name":"evals"}. Omit (or {"type":"cloud"}) for a Cursor-managed VM.

files.description: Optional file(s) to hand to a launch or reply, such as a spec, dataset, log, config, archive, or recording the cloud agent should work from. Each is saved into the agent's workspace under uploads/ and its path is listed in the prompt it receives, so it reads them with its own tools instead of you pasting contents. Documents (pdf, txt, md, csv, tsv, json, yaml, xml, html, zip, tar, gz, docx, xlsx, pptx, …) and any text file recognized by content (source, scripts, patches, or configs) up to 25 MB each, videos (mp4, mov, webm, …) up to 15 MB each, and all attachments on one call (images included) up to 46 MB together; other binary files are refused. .env-style files are refused; pass credentials with secret_names. An image here is saved as a file, not shown; use images for that. Same file:// URL rules as images: a path under /workspace or in your own attachments/assets folder.

url.description: file:// URL of the file, e.g. file:///workspace/spec.pdf.

images.description: Optional image(s) to attach to a launch or reply, such as a screenshot, mock, or chart the cloud agent needs to see. The agent sees them through its vision channel, so never paste an image as markdown in the prompt. Pass an absolute file:// URL to a file in your box: a path under /workspace or one in your own attachments/assets folder (file:///home/box/agent-data/agents/<your id>/attachments/…). https:// is not supported; download it to a file first. A non-image file goes in files, not here.

url.description: file:// URL of the image, e.g. file:///workspace/shot.png.

include_archived.description: For list: include archived agents (default false).

interrupt.description: Optional for reply. Legacy alias: true means mode: "interrupt". Prefer mode.

limit.description: For list: max agents to return (default 20).

mode.description: Optional for reply. How the follow-up reaches the agent; if omitted, the default named in the tool description's reply line applies. "queue": delivered once its current run finishes, as its next run. "steer": injected into the running turn at its next step, so the agent course-corrects with its work in flight kept; if nothing is running, it is queued instead. "interrupt": stops the running turn now (its in-flight work is lost) and starts a fresh run with the message. On an agent you did NOT launch, pass steer or interrupt only when the user explicitly asked you to redirect or interrupt that specific agent. The result says how the message was actually delivered (a steer on an idle agent is queued).

model.description: Optional model id for launch/reply. Pass only when the user explicitly requests a model override; never choose one based on the task, catalog order, or your own preference. Use the 'models' action to resolve a user-requested model name.

model_params.description: Optional structured model parameters for launch/reply, as a map of param id to string value (e.g. {"thinking":"true","effort":"xhigh"}). Requires model because parameter schemas are model-specific. Pass only for model settings the user explicitly requests; otherwise omit. Use the 'models' action to see the requested model's params, allowed values, and compatibility restrictions. Cloud agents always run in Max Mode. Booleans are the strings "true"/"false".

new_repo.description: Create a new private Origin repo and start from scratch. Prefer this for greenfield requests such as "build an app" or "start from scratch" when the user has not named an existing repo. Pass true as a JSON boolean, not the string "true".

pr_url.description: Required for find_by_pr: the pull request URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 or https://cursor.com/codebase/owner/repo/pull/123).

project.description: Launch only. true (a JSON boolean, not the string "true") starts a Project instead of a plain agent. The agent becomes the Project coordinator (see Projects). Pass true only when the user explicitly asked for a project. Omit it otherwise, including for large tasks.

prompt.description: Instruction text. Required for launch and reply.

repo.description: Required for launch unless new_repo is true or environment.type is "environment" (a saved environment supplies its own repos). Full repository URL on a GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps provider connected to the user's Cursor account (e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo or https://gitlab.com/group/project), or of an existing Cursor Origin repository. An Origin repository is passed as its https://cursor.com/codebase/owner/repo page or its origin.cursor.com clone URL (no separate connection: the signed-in Cursor account is the Origin account). A bare owner/name is rejected because it does not identify the provider; when the user gives one, look the repository up or ask where it lives, then pass the URL.

repo_name.description: Required for publish_repository: the repository name to publish the agent's Origin draft under (letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; at most 100 characters). The namespace stays the draft's own. Use the name the user confirmed.

scope.description: For list: 'launched' (default) returns only the agents you launched (or the user handed to you) in this conversation, including before any compaction; 'all' returns every cloud agent on the user's account.

search.description: Optional for repositories: a repo-name fragment (or owner/name) the source control integration matches against its own listing, e.g. 'widgets' or 'acme/widgets'. Not a regex.

secret_names.description: Optional for launch and reply. Names of this bot's own secrets (names only, never values) to set on the agent as env vars for all its runs. Later runs keep them; a reply names one only to add it or refresh its value, and only on an agent the user owns. Its tool output masks the literal values, best effort. Forward only what the task needs. Not with mode "steer".

starting_ref.description: Optional for launch. Branch or commit to start from; defaults to the repo's default branch.

title.description: Title for the cloud agent shown in the UI, used verbatim instead of the auto-generated summary of the prompt. Optional for launch; required for rename.

visibility.description: For publish_repository: who can see the published repository. PRIVATE (default when omitted): only the owner and people they add. INTERNAL: everyone in the owner's team; refused for accounts without a team. Never assume INTERNAL: ask the user with a SendToUser widget that offers both choices and pass exactly what they picked.
